utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-04-84bis-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Registrar. Could we have appearances for the day, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Daniela Kravetz for the Prosecution, with my colleagues Aditya Menon, Barbara Goy, our Case Manager Line Pedersen, and our legal intern Thomas Dutton. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for the Defence of Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Ben Emmerson for Ramush Haradinaj, together with Rod Dixon, Annie O'Reilly, and Andrew Strong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. And for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Gregor Guy-Smith on behalf of Mr. Balaj, with Ms. Rohan and Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. And for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Richard Harvey, with Mr. Luke Boenisch and Ms. Rudina Jasini.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning. Thank you so much. Mr. Emmerson -- I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we go into private -- into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we very briefly move into private session so that can I clarify one issue with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us yesterday about one meeting that you were aware of that had taken place between officers of FARK and officers of the existing KLA in the Dukagjin region shortly after your forces entered Kosovo. Do you recall giving us that evidence yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on the evidence of the senior FARK commander, I want to put to you a more detailed account of the meetings that took place and see whether you're in a position to comment on it, agree with it, or contradict it from your own knowledge. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to suggest to you that there were three meetings that took place: The first on the 25th of June, 1998, in Jasiq, at which Mr. Haradinaj was not present; the second that took place the following day, on the 26th of June, in Jasiq and then in Junik, at which Mr. Haradinaj was present; and the third which took place on the 30th of June in Junik, at which, again, Mr. Haradinaj was not present. That is the agreed evidence in this case. Are you in a position to contradict that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For your information, the first meeting -- I have information about the first meeting and the second one, but I'm not aware of a third meeting. And this might be because those days I was in Isniq village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's very helpful. You're aware, then, that Mr. Haradinaj did not attend the first meeting on the 25th of June but that he did attend the second meeting on the 26th of June; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The record is not very clear here Mr. Emmerson. Did we say Mr. Haradinaj was not present on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, he was present on the 26th. He was not present on the 25th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. 26th and 30th he was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. Just the 26th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just the 26th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us yesterday that you were not inside the room when the discussions took place on the occasion when Mr. Haradinaj attended to meet FARK officers. That's right, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in an ante-room with other ordinary rank-and-file soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While the commanders were in a separate room, out of your earshot; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during the entirety of that occasion did you speak to Mr. Haradinaj yourself at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he speak to you at any -- at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear him say anything at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Because it was a separate room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at no point on that day did you hear him say anything; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next time you saw Mr. Haradinaj was on the occasion that you've told us about in private session; is that correct? You haven't seen him between the two times.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can we take it that up until the time when you -- which you've told us about in private session, up until that date, you'd never heard him speak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll come back to that a little later on, if I may. Returning to the meeting on the 26th of June. I asked you yesterday if you understood what the disagreement between the forces was all about. And you told us that you had received an account from the FARK officers about what had been discussed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: See, I suggested to you specifically, yesterday, that there was a dispute between the two about the deployment of the FARK forces, with the KLA side, headed by Mr. Haradinaj, arguing that the FARK soldiers and officers should be distributed to reinforce and improve the existing defences that been set up, whilst the FARK brigades, under Tahir Zemaj, considered it essential that they remain as a single unit, under a single command, in one location. Remember me putting that to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just check: Are we in open session? We are. I'm seeing the Registrar nod, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you that yesterday, you said you didn't know that that was the disagreement. You've had a chance, perhaps, overnight to think about it. When you were told what had been discussed, did no one tell you that that was the central point of disagreement between the two forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was what I heard from the leaders of the FARK, the officers of the FARK, namely that the other side didn't want them to go into the deep -- to go deeper into the territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pausing there so that the Judges understand the geography: The location where FARK was at the time of these meetings, Jasik and Juniq [sic], that was, of course, on the western side of the main Pec-Decan-Djakova road, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Junik is not on that part of Peje-Decane road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. I said Junik and Jasiq are to the west of the main Pec-Decan-Djakova road, are they not? Closer to the border with Albania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the issue was whether and how the FARK forces would cross that road and enter into the territory on the eastern side; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to speak closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please get closer to the microphone when you speak because the interpreters don't hear you properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, you've been called, Mr. Witness, by the Prosecution to give some evidence about conflicts between FARK and the KLA, but I'm going to suggest to you that you have no idea what the real issues were between the two leaderships.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am speaking only about what I heard from my superiors. I said that I was never present in any of the meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you've given evidence that this was a decision by the Kosovo Liberation Army to stop FARK from entering. But that's simply not true, Witness 77. It's just not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe -- that's not my recollection of the witness evidence. And if my colleague is going to be referring to the evidence the witness gave yesterday, if we could have transcript page reference and the exact testimony be put back to the witness -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, the witness has just given the answer two minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is paraphrasing, I think, the witness evidence not correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But I'm not -- but let me see if I've got it correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday, Witness 77, and I suggest, again, this morning, that the KLA commanders were trying to stop the FARK forces entering deeper into Kosovo. Is that your understanding of what was taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not that I understood it that way, but things happened that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's get something straight, Mr. Witness. Did you just not say a few minutes ago that according to your knowledge and information from the FARK officers the KLA officers stopped the FARK troops from going deeper into the territory? You used the word "territory."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, I'm going to suggest to you -- perhaps we'll see if it can jog your memory. What you're telling us is based on what you were told, is that right, by senior commanders immediately after these meetings about what was being discussed? Is that right? Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, amongst the senior FARK commanders was the senior FARK commander that I've referred to in closed session, whose name we're not using in open session, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see if I can jog your memory about what you were told, then, by giving you his account and see if that assists your recollection of what was said to you at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that, Your Honour. Mr. Emmerson can put a proposition to the witness and ask him to agree or disagree with it, but I'm going to object to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is objectionable about that, in manner of -- of questioning?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Because he can simply -- because he's going to, in essence, be asking the witness to confirm or not confirm the evidence given by another witness. And as I had indicated earlier, this witness is only able to give evidence on matters that were -- are within his personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're not answering my question, Madam Kravetz. My question is: What's objectionable about the manner of questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It's the form of the question. If he -- my learned colleague can put a proposition to the witness and ask him to agree or disagree. But I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put to you the words of the senior FARK commander, whom you've told us that was one of your sources of information, given on oath in these -- in proceedings before this Tribunal. The disagreement was that, Mr. Haradinaj asked that senior officers be distributed in the operative units and in the villages and to carry out their tasks within the structure of the Dukagjin operational staff; however, FARK already had an established hierarchy and was not in a position to do such a thing, to systemise 23 officers and destroy the structure they entered with. This was the friction.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Reference: Transcript, T761494 and following.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then I'll just give you another quotation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this transcript --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: From the first trial, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another quotation: Ramush met with us when we crossed into Kosovo. The meeting was on the 26th of June, 1998, in Jasiq. Ramush was there to inform FARK that there was an active Dukagjini staff at the time and that FARK should become a part of that structure. At the same time FARK had its own command which was the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Kosova and as professional soldiers it was difficult to change plans. This created a friction.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is transcript 756091 and following. End quotation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you take it quotation by quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I certainly will do. But perhaps I can put the specific proposition to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before you do that - just to make sure that I understand this - is this the testimony of the senior commander about what happened in the meeting room or what was said in the meeting room?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Or is this his testimony about what he told the men in the ante-room?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, this is his testimony about what actually happened in the meeting room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the question I'm asking you, Witness 77, is whether you were aware that the real source of the dispute was not that the KLA wanted to keep FARK out of Kosovo but that they wanted to distribute the FARK forces in a particular way within Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is this a question for me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I think -- having heard the evidence of the senior FARK commander, I'm inviting you to re-examine your recollection and to tell the Chamber whether it really is the case that you were told that this was the KLA trying to prevent FARK forces from entering, or the KLA trying to agree how they should be distributed when they entered. You can understand the difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand the difference. That was what I heard from the senior commanders. But, as far as I know, they didn't agree to be placed under the structure under the command of the KLA because they were representing the forces of the Republic of Kosova. They didn't want to be placed under the command of others, because these others were people who were not familiar with the military art, and that's why they refused to be distributed to other brigades of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did know, then, that that was the source of the disagreement, the manner of distribution? You knew that; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you tell us yesterday that you didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't asked the question, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you that question yesterday afternoon, Witness 77, quite specifically. I put it to you that the distribution of FARK forces within Kosovo was the source of the disagreement, and you said: Not as far as you were aware.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember saying that. Maybe it's a human mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to present a certain picture to the Tribunal here? Are you trying to create a picture of conflict as between the two forces which is different from the reality, Witness 77?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not trying to do that. The reason why I gave the answer that I gave was maybe because I didn't get the question. I didn't understand the question clearly. And that's what I heard from the officers, that they didn't want to be distributed. And that's why, after that, they were asked to leave Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read you a passage of your testimony yesterday, Witness 77. This is page 1219, line 24 and following. I asked you this question: "I'm suggesting to you that there was a dispute between the commanders of FARK, including Tahir Zemaj, and the commanders of the KLA inside Kosovo, including Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Maloku, about the deployment of FARK soldiers. And I can put it a bit more specifically. "Those who were already organised on the ground inside Kosovo wanted the FARK brigades to be distributed amongst the already organising village defence units, whereas the FARK commanders under Zemaj considered it essential that all of the 225 FARK officers remain together and in one place? "That was the dispute, wasn't it?" To which you answered: "I don't believe so. I don't know." Why did you say "I don't believe so" yesterday, when you're now telling us that you knew that that was the dispute, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There existed a disagreement. But yesterday when I said I don't know, I didn't remember. Maybe my memory was refreshed today. I don't think this is a bad thing. I remember that there were two options given to them; either they go under the command of Haradinaj and Maloku, or turn back to Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, I'm going to suggest to you, Mr. Witness, that you've come here, as your evidence shows - I'm going to put it to you - that you've come here with an agenda to seek to discredit Mr. Haradinaj. What's your response to that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've not come here to discredit anyone. I am simply recounting here what I know. I'm not here to seek revenge. I'm here to seek justice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You understand that you've given a solemn declaration, don't you, and you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. That's why I'm here. I won't speak any word that I don't know or I haven't heard said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, when I ask you specifically was it your understanding that a particular event occurred and you say no, when, in fact, the answer is yes, do you understand that that is not consistent with your oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it does -- it is consistent. Because I'm here to speak the truth and only the truth, what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think that if you say the opposite of the truth that is consistent with your oath; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You sought, I suggest, yesterday, to create the impression that Ramush Haradinaj and the Kosovo Liberation Army forces were being obstructive. That was your intention in the testimony you gave yesterday. Is that right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. That's my impression. And all the other commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to, again, see if it jogs your memory about what you were told by the FARK commanders concerning Mr. Haradinaj's attitude. I'm going to read to you again from the testimony of the senior FARK commander who was present inside that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this is transcript 7613, line 19. "Q. Now, you describe in your witness statement Mr. Haradinaj, in that meeting of the 26th of June, you describe him as being controlled an orderly. Is that an accurate description? "A. Yes, a very accurate description. He was a very constructive, moderate, this is the impression that I got." Was that the impression that was conveyed to you, Witness 77, that Mr. Haradinaj was controlled, orderly, constructive, and moderate in that meeting? Because you've told us that he was obstructive, as you understood it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I know is the words that I heard from my officers. I was not in the meeting, and I don't know who said what in the meeting. These words I only hear from you here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You see, you gave evidence without that information available to you, but I'm going to suggest to you again you have deliberately tried to create a misleading impression to the Trial Chamber that Mr. Haradinaj's position was obstructive, when, in fact, it was quite the reverse.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: My learned colleague is putting a question he has already put to the witness which the witness has answered. It's just put a different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm putting it on the basis of yet further evidence that the witness is misleading the Chamber, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not evidence. That's what you're suggesting to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm making the suggestion based on now the fact that not only has he misled the Chamber about his state of knowledge concerning what the essence of the dispute was, but that he's now mislead the Chamber, I suggest, about the nature of what was said to him concerning Mr. Haradinaj's so-suggested -- what is suggested to be an obstructive attitude towards the FARK forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, in my view that is really a matter for submissions to be made at a later stage when my learned colleague addresses matters regarding this witness evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm perfectly, with respect, entitled to explore the credibility of this witness, and that's what I'm doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us yesterday and now, in terms this morning, that you understood Mr. Haradinaj to have been obstructive in those discussions, is that information you say you got from the senior FARK commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. I was not in the meeting personally, and I am repeating this for several times now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we've now, as you have heard, there has been direct evidence from somebody who was the senior FARK commander in the meeting to precisely the opposite effect. The question I'm asking you, Witness 77, is whether you are making up what you are saying in order to create a misleading impression to the Tribunal, because the source of the information, the senior FARK commander, has given this Tribunal, on oath, contradictory evidence to that which you say came to you from the senior FARK commanders who were present?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your question asked and answered, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Just to -- I couldn't help overhearing the sotto voce comment. Yes, that is the answer the witness gave. I'm suggesting that he's lying. That's all I want to explore. I'm suggest that the witness is deliberately giving this Chamber a misleading impression of what he was told, given that we have it from the horse's mouth as to what the truth was and given that the witness himself has already acknowledged that he gave the Tribunal evidence yesterday that he did not know that the nature of the dispute was about constructive deployment, whereas he now tells us that he did. There are in circumstances such as that -- perfectly proper to explore whether he is deliberately misleading the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, it may very well be that the witness is misleading the Chamber. It may very well be that the witness heard what he heard from whomever he heard it, which is different from the senior FARK commander. I think you have made your point that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, may I ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've made your point that what he says he knows is different from what the senior commander told this -- the Tribunal in -- the Trial Chamber in the previous case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, but also what he says he knows is different from what he said he knew yesterday, on oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, and that you have established.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to the senior FARK commander, the man whom we've named in private session? Did you speak to him about these meetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean, "did you speak to him"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that after the meeting you received a report from the senior FARK commanders, and I'm asking you whether amongst those who you spoke to about the meeting was the senior FARK commander?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague Mr. Emmerson has referred to three meetings when he's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If the witness could wait. He's referred to three meetings when he started this line of question. If we could have a clarification as to which meeting exactly he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If Ms. Kravetz follows the evidence, there's only one meeting at which Mr. Haradinaj was present. So there's only one meeting that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us, Witness 77, that after that meeting you received information from the FARK officers who had been in the meeting, and I'm asking you whether you received information or discussed the meeting with the senior FARK commander?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I still consider it's necessary for my learned colleague to clarify which of the meetings he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's the meeting that was attended by Mr. Haradinaj, Madam Kravetz. And the witness knows that, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: There is a difference, though, between the -- the villages that have been mentioned, so I think it's still important to refer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is -- what have villages got to do with the meeting? The meeting is the meeting that was attended by Mr. Haradinaj. There were three meetings, two of which he didn't attend. And they have gone through that part of the evidence with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Maybe -- if the witness could remove his head phones, I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me make it clear. It will save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Then it's -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the meeting attended by Mr. Haradinaj, and you've told us you saw him walk into a room where a meeting took place. And you've told us that after that meeting you received information from the FARK commanders who were in the meeting about what was being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you give him the date, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date is the 25th -- I'm sorry, the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But he -- I think the witness is unaware of dates but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The meeting at which Mr. Haradinaj was present, where you've told us you saw him walk into the room, you remained in an ante-chamber, and afterwards, you've told us, you received information from the FARK officers about what had been discussed? And the question I'm asking you is this: Amongst the FARK officers giving that information, was the named senior FARK commander - and you know who I'm referring to - was he one of your sources of information? Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... just before you comment the question, I see Madam Kravetz is on her feet. Yes, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The problem with the way the question is being put is that Mr. Emmerson has referred to the testimony of the senior FARK commander, and it is not clear from the evidence he has given and the evidence the witness has given that we're talking about the same meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Absolutely --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So that's why I'm asking if you could just clarify --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's absolutely clear. And if Ms. Kravetz is remotely familiar with the evidence, she would know this. There was only one meeting attended by Mr. Haradinaj, as the senior FARK commander himself testified. And if Ms. Kravetz has read his testimony, she would know that. So he is referring to that meeting. This witness is referring to that meeting. There is no conceivable possibility for misunderstanding. Thank you. So this is simply obstructionist objections. If Ms. Kravetz knows the evidence, she wouldn't be making that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask the question to you again, Witness 77. Was the senior FARK commander one of those you spoke to about the meeting that had taken place with Mr. Haradinaj; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander that you spoke to, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a more senior commander than the one you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... can I have his name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I received the information from Colonel Tahir Zemaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Because you're aware that Colonel Tahir Zemaj has written about this meeting in publications, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Have you never read anything that Colonel Tahir Zemaj wrote about these meetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Finally this, on this topic. The evidence of the senior FARK commander - and I'm quoting transcript T7614, line 15 - is as follows, and this relates to both of the first two meetings the 25th and 26th: "At those first two meetings there were differences of opinion but there were constructive discussions about how to move forward and accommodate the new force. Both sides wanted to reach an agreement but neither was ready to abandon its position." Is that a fair summary of what you understood the position to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the matter stood like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so why did you tell us that the position of the KLA was obstructive then, just a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An agreement was not reached. And, as I said earlier, the FARK forces were told to go back where they came from because they wouldn't be allowed to go deeper into Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a third meeting in Junik on the 30th of June, and, again, no agreement was reached; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because at that stage you were in Isniq; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, you told us yesterday that there was a gap of ten days between the meeting attended by Mr. Haradinaj and the entry of the FARK forces. But that's simply not right, is it? FARK forces entered on the 30th of June, four days after the meeting with Mr. Haradinaj, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can't remember something, Witness, when somebody asks you how long it was, you say, "I can't remember." What you don't say is, "It was ten days," if you do not know. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you say ten days?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we have a transcript page reference where the witness said --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'll have that looked out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- that there were ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll have it looked out, the transcript reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you say ten days?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we have the transcript reference before we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll take a pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Page 1163, line 1. Again, I would ask Ms. Kravetz to keep her objections reasonable, because this is simply time-taking. The question is from Ms. Kravetz herself, 1163, line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Emmerson, I'm not quite sure what you are saying about Madam Kravetz. She only asked for a page reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But the reality is I wouldn't have put the question without having a sound basis for doing it. I indicated that I was perfectly happy to look up the reference and provide it, instead of which we lose -- we lose minutes in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But for her also to be able to prepare her re-examination you need to give a page reference at the time when you quote it. You can't say you're going to have it looked up, Mr. Emmerson. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. 1163. "Q. And when you say that these officers, that is, Tahir Zemaj and the other officers, were not welcome, whom are you referring to when you say they were not welcome? By whom were they not welcome? "A. As I said, in the meeting there were three people, Ramush, Naim Maloku, and the third person. "Q. Have you completed your answer, sir? I was asking: Who did not welcome Tahir Zemaj and the other officers? "A. Ramush, Naim Maloku, and the third person. "Q. Thank you. I think now it's clear. "As a result of this meeting between Ramush Haradinaj, Tahir Zemaj, and the other officers you've referred to, did the FARK forces leave the village of Jasiq? "A. No. "Q. For how long did they remain in that village? "A. For about ten days, I would say. "Q. And after those ten days, where did these [sic] forces go? "A. They remained there until Sali Ceku, Ismet Ceku ... and myself --" "Q. Can I stop you there --" And then we enter private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I go back to the question my learned colleague was putting to the witness - and this is today's transcript page 24, line 20 - he put to the witness: "You see, you told us yesterday there was a gap of ten days between the meeting attended by Haradinaj and the entry of FARK forces." That is very different from the evidence that Mr. Emmerson has just -- from yesterday that Mr. Emmerson has just read out to the witness. So the reference to the ten days had to do from when --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before my learned friend gives evidence, perhaps we can ask the witness what he meant by it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said yesterday that the forces of FARK were in Jasiq for ten days, you were asked the question how long they remained. Let me just put the question to you in terms: "As a result of this meeting between Ramush Haradinaj, Tahir Zemaj, and the other officers you've referred to, as a result of that meeting, did the FARK forces leave? "No. "For how long did they remain in that village? "A. For about ten days. What did you mean by "for about ten days"? From when till when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can see here, I am not very clear of the question. I think you're asking a different question now than what asked before. If the question before was how many days they remained in Jasiq, I said ten days, approximately. I don't think the question was put to me the way you are putting it to me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me put the question to you now then. How long after the meeting with Mr. Haradinaj do you say that FARK forces entered Kosovo -- sorry, moved from the area on the western side of the road to the eastern side of the road in Isniq?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately ten days, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, what I'm putting to you is that the FARK forces entered four days later, on the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we're back where we started. And I'm suggesting to you that if you don't know the answer to something you should not give a time estimate. If somebody says to you, "How long between the meeting and the move to Jasiq," do you understand that if you don't know the answer, you should say, "I don't know," rather than say it's ten days, when you're not in a position to contradict the submission that it's four?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm a bit confused with the question. It has changed a couple of times. My learned colleague was asking about the move from Jasiq to Isniq and now he's asking from the entry of the FARK to the move to Jasiq.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The time-period -- I mean, it's not very clear what the ten days referred to, whether the entry of FARK forces into Kosovo and then to Jasiq or whether the move from Jasiq to Isniq. It has been stated in two ways by Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have probably seen it stated in three ways. I'm not quite sure that I'm following, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me clarify, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: May I add, Mr. Emmerson, that the witness answer was not ten days. The witness answer was "about ten days," approximately --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Approximately ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I accept that. But four days -- it's a matter of opinion, but four days may not be thought be approximately ten days, in terms of accuracy and reliability. Part of Your Honours' function is to determine the reliability of the witness, whether information that he gives can be relied upon. And if one looks at the transcript - and I did make it absolutely clear, so there should be no misunderstanding - Ms. Kravetz sought to suggest that the reference I made to the transcript yesterday was unfair because, in fact, maybe the witness was saying ten days in total, rather than ten days from the time of the meeting until the entry to Isniq. So I asked the witness just a moment ago, at page 27, line 16: "How long after the meeting with Mr. Haradinaj do you say ... FARK forces entered Kosovo ... moved from the area on the western side of the road to the eastern side ..." "Approximately ten days ..." Now, if that needs clarification, I'll ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem with how the question was put, on page 28, line 1, because there he talks about how long between the meeting and the move to Jasiq, and then it says: "... do you understand that if you don't understand [sic] the answer, you should say so." That is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- that is the confusion that I'm pointing at.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think that's a transcription error because I think the question I asked was Isniq. But I'll put it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say ten days, Witness 77, are you referring to the ten-day estimate between the meeting and the time when the FARK forces moved to Isniq?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've given us a ten-day period from the date of the meeting. Is it a period of ten days that you say is the time between the date of the meeting with Mr. Haradinaj and the date of the move to Isniq?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I hope it's clear now for Ms. Kravetz. Can we move --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one further question. When the movement took place, whatever date it was - and I'm suggesting to you it was on the 30th of June - did the FARK forces entering or moving towards Isniq, did that involve them crossing the main Peja-Decan-Djakova road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you had to pass through that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the FARK forces enter marching under a KLA banner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the banner of the brigade, the 134rd Brigade of the KLA. The emblems of the soldiers were red UCK/KLA, not FARK, as it's being said now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So that we're clear, so the Tribunal understand: They entered wearing Kosovo Liberation Army/UCK insignia, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the soldiers regard themselves as being part of the same force as the UCK inside Kosovo or a different force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can speak only on behalf of myself, not of the others. I considered myself as a soldier of the Liberation Army of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't make any distinction, myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you wearing KLA insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you, in fact, march through the village of Gllogjan, or, rather, did the forces March through the village of Gllogjan on their way to Isniq?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my recollection, they marched. Because I myself was in Isniq. The forces marched up to the village of Rexhe, as far as I know. Then there were some trucks that went to fetch them. Some lorries took them and transported them to Isniq.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was: Did the FARK forces pass through the village of Gllogjan en route to Isniq?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly they did. Because that was the only open route.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were permitted to pass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They arrived in Isniq in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to now move beyond the incident that was dealt with in private session, because I'll deal with that towards the end. I want to move forwards now, please, to the time when the FARK forces moved from Isniq to Prapaqan. First of all, how long after their arrival, in your estimation, did the FARK forces remain in Isniq before they moved to Prapaqan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't be precise. I don't recall very well. I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether it was days or weeks? Or months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I might say for some weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The barracks in Prapaqan had been newly equipped by the Kosovo Liberation Army in the Dukagjini plain, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was not a single equipment in that school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there beds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village helped -- a nearby village helped, Dubovik village helped, to prepare some beds within a very short time, but the school had nothing in terms of equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Rrustem Tetaj yesterday, and you said that he was the commander in Lluke. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj testified before this Tribunal that the funding for the Prapaqan barracks had been provided to him by Mr. Haradinaj and then made available to the FARK brigades. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we have a reference for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Last trial: 3755, line 14; 3750, line 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that these barracks had been earmarked by Mr. Haradinaj and funding provided in order to house the FARK brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. I don't even believe that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Well, correct me if I'm wrong, but Mr. Tetaj testified that he organised for the FARK soldiers to stay in Prapaqan. Is that right or not, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's better if I say I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know, it certainly is better that you say you don't know. But were you there when the move to Prapaqan took place, when the forces of the FARK arrived at Prapaqan? Were you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Skender Rexhahmetaj, who testified in this trial, and Rrustem Tetaj, who testified in the last trial, were there to meet the FARK forces and welcome them to the Prapaqan barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Prapaqan barracks had been provided as a result of an agreement between Tahir Zemaj and Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know of any agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The facility, I suggest, was made available to you in Prapaqan so that you could move from Isniq - you being the FARK forces - was made available to you by Mr. Haradinaj and his subzone commanders Mr. Tetaj and Mr. Rexhahmetaj; you were given it by the KLA, I suggest. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not only that, but there were already KLA soldiers stationed in the Prapaqan barracks when you arrived who were then integrated within your FARK brigade. That's right, isn't it? You must know that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you? I thought you were in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was recovering, sir, at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you recovering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Isniq.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Prapaqan at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you've told us about an incident that took place at Prapaqan, haven't you, a confrontation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were there, then. That happened within a couple of days of the arrival of the FARK forces, didn't it, that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember accurately when it occurred, but I know how it occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... would that be a convenient moment, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Indeed, Your honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To do so, may the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson -- I beg your pardon. May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 77, I want to go back now to the dates, please, and the chronology of the move to Prapaqan just so the Trial Chamber has the accurate picture. I'm going to suggest to you - and there is agreed evidence to this effect - that the date upon which the FARK forces moved from the west side of the road to Isniq was the 30th of June, after the last meeting in Junik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may be. I don't recall very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, again, I'm going to suggest to you that the date of the move to the barracks at Prapaqan which had been provided to the FARK soldiers by the KLA under the command of Ramush Haradinaj was the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may be. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you told us earlier on, when pressed, you thought that the FARK forces had been stationed at Isniq for weeks. In fact, the agreed evidence is that they were stationed at Isniq for one week and two days. That's evidence admitted by agreement from the previous trial. So if you could just clarify: You're not in a position to contradict that, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not. I don't recall very well. I thought that they stayed there one or two weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just so that we're clear: The incident which we're going to ask some questions about in private session, that occurred between those two dates, between the entry into -- into Isniq on the 30th of June and the move to Prapaqan on the 9th of July, it was during that period that that incident occurred. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've also referred to a confrontation that took place at the Prapaqan barracks in which Mr. Haradinaj attended and expelled the officers, leaving the soldiers behind. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, the unchallenged evidence is that that incident occurred on the 10th of July, the day after the move to the Prapaqan barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot challenge that because I don't remember very well the date. But I know that I was there. The date, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you were there on the 10th of July, you were certainly in Prapaqan the day after the move of the FARK forces to the Prapaqan barracks. Does that help you work out whether you were there on the day of the move? You've told us a little earlier on you were not there because you were still recovering in Isniq.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was recovering, that's true. But I don't think it was one day after, as you said, as you put to me. I can't confirm it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a very, very considerable body of other evidence in this case which confirms that it was the 9th of July that the move took place, and there's a very considerable body of other evidence all agreed that the incident, the confrontation, took place on the 10th of July. Indeed, there are minutes of a meeting that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The witness has already indicated that he can't confirm the date when this occurred. He has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, what I'm trying to do, Your Honours, to isolate when he arrived at Prapaqan. There's only one day possible, and I just want to understand whether he arrived on the day of the move or on the day of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I believe he has already answered that as well, and he has already indicated that he does not remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me put the question another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you were there on the 10th of July when the confrontation took place, at which --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That is not a correct statement of the witness evidence. The witness does not remember when the confrontation took place. He has already indicated he does not remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let's put it this way: There is absolutely no dispute between the parties that the confrontation took place on the 10th of July. And without going into all of the evidence which in due course will be available to the Trial Chamber, there are minutes, recorded minutes, of the meeting that followed from that incident that day. So there's no doubt at all that the incident took place on the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my question is - you say you were there at Prapaqan when that incident took place - my question is: Did you arrive there that day or had you arrived there before then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I know that I was in the Prapaqan barracks for some days by then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying you had been in Prapaqan for some days, you, yourself, had been physically present in Prapaqan in the barracks for some days before the confrontation which the officers were expelled; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you that on all of the evidence that cannot be the truth, Witness 77, because we have independent and confirmed and agreed evidence that the FARK did not move to the barracks until the day before that incident. So I'm going to ask you to examine your recollection again. Are you sure you were there for some days before that incident took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my recollection, I was in Prapaqan barracks before that incident occurred, and I'm repeating it. This is how I remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's important that you understand, as I said to you earlier on, the need to give accurate evidence according to your oath. And I'm going to suggest to you that the evidence will prove incontrovertibly that what you've just said cannot be true. And so I'm going to invite you again to examine whether you are sure that you had been there for some days before the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. My learned colleague has put this question to the witness repeatedly in different forms. The witness has already said - and the latest answer is on page 38, line 12 - that to his recollection he was there before the incident occurred. Now, it's a matter for submissions --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, just --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- at a later stage --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- whether the witness recollection is right or not. This is his recollection, and he has responded to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With respect, it's not solely a matter of recollection. If this witness is not telling the truth, that's something I'm entitled to explore. And as Your Honour also find in due course, the chronology that I've outlined is incontrovertible and agreed. It follows that the witness cannot be right when he says that he had been there for several days. Now, what I want to do is to give him an opportunity to say whether he may be mistaken or whether he insists on the position that he is taking. And it's no good Ms. Kravetz saying he was there before the incident. His testimony is he was there some days before the incident. A multiple of days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The problem, Madam Kravetz, is that I think in the last --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say some days, it may be two or three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the witness is taking what I was going to say out of my mouth. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were certainly there the day before the incident; you're sure of that, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if it is the position that everybody in this trial is agreed on the evidence that the incident took place on the 10th of July, it follows you were definitely there on 9th of July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said two or three. You didn't say one or two. So does it follow you were there on the 8th of July as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has already indicated that he's not clear as to the dates when he was there. He has provided an answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- that's simply wrong. He's just said he's sure that he was there on the 9th. And I'm asking him, is he also sure he was there on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That was an answer following a question, which said: If it's the position that everybody in this trial is agreed that the incident took place on the 10th of July, it follows that you were definitely there on the 9th of July. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It is the position that everyone in this trial is agreed that the incident took place on the 10th of July, and Ms. Kravetz ought to know that. Therefore I'm asking whether the witness is reserving to himself some area of uncertainty about the 8th or whether he is committing himself to saying he is sure he was there. Plainly, that has different ramifications for his credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Overruled, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you've told us you were definitely there on the 9th. Were you definitely there on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible that I was there on the 8th. I can't remember, though. I told you that I'm not very good with dates. But I know that I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If, as you've told us, you're sure you were there on the 9th, then you were there on the very day FARK forces moved into Prapaqan barracks, I suggest. So perhaps you would assist us with your recollection of that significant event.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I was there the day when the FARK forces entered the barracks. I -- I can't recollect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll check the transcript. Because I thought before the break you said you were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps somebody could check that, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break I asked you that question, and you said you were not there, not that you couldn't remember one way or the other. What is the position: Were you there, were you not there, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I was there the day of the incident but I can't remember the date. My dates are not coinciding with yours. I told you that I was in Prapaqan. I'm sure that I was there. I've not come here to make up stories or to lie, as you said earlier. I'm describing you the reality the way I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 77, please don't try and shelter behind your uncertainty about dates. I'm asking you about events, not dates. And I'm asking you very clearly whether you were there on that very significant day when the FARK forces moved in to the barracks at Prapaqan. Before the break, you told us, categorically, that you were not. When I've put the dates to you, you are now saying that you don't know whether you were or you weren't. What is the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say I was not there. I said I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, transcript page 32, line 14. Question, line 12: "But were you there when the move to Prapaqan took place, when the forces of the FARK arrived at Prapaqan? Were you there? "A. No."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you say "no" before the break, Witness 77, if you're now telling us you don't know one way or the other whether you were there? Why did you deny it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not denying it. I said that it is possible that I've forgotten. I know that I was there, but I don't know what days. And it is possible that I went there in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't tell us that you weren't sure before the break, Witness 77. You didn't know one way or the other, you couldn't remember. You were categorical in saying you were not there when the FARK forces arrived at Prapaqan. What is your evidence: Were you there, were you not there, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The witness has just answered that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me put it another way, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said a moment ago in answer to that question that what you had said was that you didn't know. In fact, as you will see from the transcript, what you said was that you did know and that you were not there. Why did you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not there when the forces arrived. Maybe I arrived in the afternoon. I can't remember exactly. But what I'm sure is that I was there on the date of the incident. I'm not sure about the other days, but I was there -- the dates -- the other dates, but I was there on the date of the incident. I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... asking you about the date of the incident. I'm asking you about the arrival of the forces in Prapaqan. So now you're telling us you were not there when the forces arrived. Earlier on, just after the break, you said you didn't know whether you were there or not. What's the truth? It's important, this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The witness has answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, he's answered it in many different ways. I'd like to have a clear answer from him, a final answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: He has just given that answer. It's at line 15 -- it starts at line 15 of page forty -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's in conflict to the answer that he gave earlier on, and I wish to know which is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: He has provided an explanation. He's been put the questions several times and he has just provided an explanation of why he said what he said before and is responding to the question as he is doing so now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Kravetz, I'm sorry, I'm going to rule you out of order because -- and, I'm afraid, the witness has been jumping from one position to another. And I'm not quite sure what is his actual position right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I think it is important -- if all this is of great importance, it is important to make the difference between the question "were you there" and the day --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I've understood that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've understood that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- when they arrive or were you there when they arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've been very careful to make that distinction --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- in the course of the questions I've asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On reflection on the transcript, Your Honour will see I've been very, very careful to make that distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If that's clear to the witness as well, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the question I'm asking, once and for all, final answer please: When the FARK forces arrived in the barracks for the first time, were you there or were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as you've already told us, if the agreed evidence is right, you must have been there that day, later on at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On that one he said he might have arrived in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... yes, but he must have been there on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct? You've already told us you were sure you were there on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you that I can't remember the dates. It is possible that I did not arrive there the same time the forces arrived. I might have arrived there in the afternoon. That's what I told you earlier. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us that you thought you were there for two or three days before the incident on the 10th. But now you're saying you might have arrived on the afternoon of the 9th. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think you have made your point on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the -- on the basis of that, it follows, Witness 77, that you were certainly there within hours of the arrival of the FARK forces in Prapaqan; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not arrive there before the forces. I never said that. The way you're putting the dates to me, I can't say anything accurate about them. But what I remember is that I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just put it this way to you: You've told us that you're categorically sure that you were there at some time on the day before the incident. And so what I'm asking you, given what we know about the date of the arrival of the FARK forces, is this: When the FARK forces arrived, there were already KLA soldiers stationed inside the Prapaqan barracks, which were then going to be shared; correct or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe that. I did not see them myself. I never heard that when they arrived there were already military forces in the barracks. If I had heard that, I would have told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be mistaken about that, Witness 77, bearing in mind that there is other evidence in this case concerning that? Could you be mistaken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I never heard that when the FARK forces arrived at the barracks there were other soldiers already there. And I'm not sure what answer you want from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you again: As you arrive, yourself, at Prapaqan, you know the soldiers that came in with FARK, and I'm suggesting that since you clearly arrived on the very same day, whether before or after, you arrived on the very same day in Prapaqan as the FARK forces, were you not aware that there was a process of integration taking place between the FARK forces and the KLA forces that were already stationed there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I think, Mr. Emmerson, the witness said, at page 45, lines 9: "I don't believe that. I did not see them myself. I never heard that when they arrived there were already military forces in the barracks. If I had heard that, I would have told you." Now, I think he has answered that question clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The only question I want to batten down with him is, given the number of different answer this witness has given to all of the important questions of fact so far, I want to know whether he is pinning his colours to that mast --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- or whether he is saying he could be mistaken in his recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that answer suggests that he could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the 9th of July. Then on the 10th of July there is a conflict which took place. And you've described in your evidence the fact that the officers were directed to leave the Prapaqan barracks and the soldiers of the FARK permitted to remain. Now, do you remember, or did you know, even, why it was that the officers were being directed to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly why. The person who wanted to expel them should know that. I gave you my personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So anything you've told us about that incident and its reasons was a matter of your opinion, was that correct, rather than any evidence that you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never heard any evidence. I just gave you my personal opinion why that might have happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I think your question was a little unfair, to say everything you've told us is a matter of opinion. He opines only on this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I thought I'd made that clear. Anything you've told us about that incident and its reasons. I should have said: Anything you've told us about the reasons for that incident. But I think the answer is clear. It doesn't require further questions. Does Your Honour agree, at least, in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's helpful. So you're not in a position to contradict the suggestion that there was a disagreement about the deployment of the officers and that that was what lay at the heart of the conflict on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which suggestion do you want me to contradict?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I don't want to you contradict anything. I'm saying: Given that you don't know what the nature of the dispute was, you're not in a position to contradict me telling you or suggesting to you that this was a dispute about deployment of the officers and about their conduct inside the Prapaqan barracks. [Microphone not activated] ... you don't know what it was about. You don't know; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the reason behind that. I told you that I know that I was present when Haradinaj and his team of military police came and expelled the officers. But I didn't say that I knew the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm just clarifying that you don't know the reason. See, we've heard evidence in the previous trial, agreed in this trial to be admitted from Rrustem Tetaj who was present, as you told us, on that occasion, who said: "... we were there when Ramush spoke and I spoke. They," the officers, "left the barracks because they admitted that they were not implementing the rules there at that moment, at that time." Transcript 3756, line 13, previous trial.
