The officers were, it is suggested, directed to leave and admitted that they were not implementing the rules that had been agreed. You don't know whether that's right or wrong, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has already said that he does not know the reason behind that, and he can't comment on this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: On the basis of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think that specific suggestion has been put to him thus far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is: Are you in a position to contradict the evidence of Rrustem Tetaj, that the officers of the FARK admitted that they had broken the rules and that that was the reason given for their expulsion from the Prapaqan barracks? Are you in a position to contradict that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It follows ipso facto, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours are content to take it at that, then I'm content to leave it there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Give it a moment. Can you hear me now in a language that you understand, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If Your Honours are content to accept that the position is that this witness is not able to contradict that, then I'm prepared to leave the matter there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's the 10th. But in the afternoon of the 10th, after that incident occurred, you do know, don't you, that there was then a meeting between Tahir Zemaj, Ramush Haradinaj, and other senior officers on both sides at Lluke?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that that meeting, that afternoon, that very same afternoon, the 10th of July --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which, for Your Honours's note, is minuted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that that meeting was arranged to resolve the disagreement that had blown up that morning. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that meeting -- presumably you were not present, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you told about what happened and what was agreed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had no idea after the -- the date of the 10th what had been agreed between the two commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then did that remain the position thereafter forever, that you had no idea what they'd agreed? Or did there come a time when you did become aware what had been agreed between them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never knew exactly what was talked about in the meeting. The main thing was that the officers had agreed, but I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never mind the details. What, as you understood it, had they agreed to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had agreed on several things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, they had divided up the territories, which area would be under the Haradinaj staff and which territory would be under the FARK staff, and they would not mix the two with each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, that last comment isn't true, I suggest. Whether you thought it or not, it's not true. Because on the 12th of July - and the Trial Chamber has this in the record - there are orders signed by Ramush Haradinaj, creating integrated brigades which included FARK soldiers and KLA soldiers in a single brigade. That is the position objectively. Are you telling me you didn't know that the brigades were being integrated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, I'm just trying to understand what you were aware of, Witness 77, about the force that you say you were a part of. Which brigade were you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 134rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who was the commander of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tahir Zemaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, after the formation of the brigades that were created following the meeting of the 10th of July, there were three separate brigades formed, which, I suggest, were integrated between KLA and FARK forces. And I'm asking you who: Was the commander of the particular brigade that you were attached to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one I explained to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell me who Shaban Dragaj was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was one of the officers that entered at the same time as the 134rd Brigade. I mean entered Kosovo at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was part of the FARK commander group, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Musa Gjakova, also one of the FARK commanders; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not know that they were integrated into a single brigade on the 12th of July, together with Shemsedin Cekaj and Driton Zeneli as KLA commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we have all the records, Witness 77. You know who Shemsedin Cekaj was, don't you? He was a member of the KLA forces and a subzone commander under Mr. Haradinaj. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're telling us you didn't know that as of the 12th of July he was in joint command with Shaban Dragaj of one of the brigades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who was integrated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for names. Do you know or did you know that the two forces were integrated into joint brigades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't know. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 77, you need to tread very carefully at this point. Your brigade was under the command of Tahir Zemaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Skender Rexhahmetaj, was he connected to these joint brigades at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was the commander in Isniq village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, amongst the exhibits in this case is 65 ter 192, which is a request by Tahir Zemaj in writing to the Dukagjini plain operative staff for the appointment of certain individuals to certain posts. Now, you know who the Dukagjini plain operational staff was, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Well, what I want to suggest to you, in absolutely unequivocal terms, Witness 77, is that the agreed, recorded, independent evidence in this case establishes that as of the 10th of July meeting at Lluke the two forces integrated into joint brigades with commanders and soldiers from both sides and then were distributed by agreement to different locations. That is, in fact, the position. Are you saying you didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The question has already been put to the witness. He has already indicated what is the extent of his knowledge and he has already indicated that he was not privy to any of the meetings where these matters were discussed and has indicated what his position within these forces was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the question I'm asking is: Can you -- how can you possibly have been unaware that there was a integration taking place and that Tahir Zemaj had agreed with Ramush Haradinaj to create joint brigades? How can you not have known that, if you were one of the soldiers in those brigades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you earlier that I was just a foot soldier. But, to my knowledge, these brigades were a continuation of Brigade 134, the brigade in Baran, and the brigade commanded by Musa Gjakova in Palabardhe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you a line from the evidence of the FARK commander in the previous trial about the formation of these brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for Your Honours' note, Exhibits 247 and 248, which I don't propose to trouble the witness with, given his account, are contemporary records showing the formation of joint brigades at this time and in consequence of this meeting between the 10th and the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to that, the senior FARK commander that you've told us about testified to this Tribunal that those brigades were formed -- I'm sorry, those brigades that formed were made up of FARK officers as well as the officers already inside Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's transcript T7438 [sic], line 19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you were a member of one of these brigades, and given that you'd entered Kosovo just a few -- couple of weeks before, together with the FARK officers, and given that the position was objectively and factually greed to be one of integration, is there anything about you or your role or functions which could possibly have insulated you from that knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is the same question, only put in a different way, that was asked at page 53, line 2. He has been asked: How could you not have known, if you were one of the soldiers of that -- those brigades?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'll check the -- let me put --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... same question and --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... let me put the question. I'll take the objection. Let me put the question another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this another example, Witness 77, of you trying to mislead this Tribunal to create a negative impression of the conflict between FARK and the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That is a completely unfair statement to the witness, and it is a matter for submissions. If my colleague wants to make submission on the credibility of the witness, that's really a matter for submissions at a later stage. The witness has already indicated what is his knowledge on this matter. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not confined to exploring the witness's knowledge. I'm perfectly entitled to put the suggestion to him that he's misleading the Tribunal, as he has, in our submission, throughout his evidence on a number of these points. And he's deliberately created the impression and indeed said in terms just a few moments ago in his evidence that these were separate brigades without integration, when the evidence flies completely in the face of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just rule, please. You rephrased your question, Mr. Emmerson, by saying: "Is this another example, Witness 77, of you trying to mislead this Tribunal to creat a negative impression of the conflict between FARK and the KLA?" I'll allow that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to mislead the Tribunal by creating a spin, a misleading spin, on the evidence, Witness 77?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On the contrary. I am saying what I know. Because I took a solemn oath, and I have to abide but that, to tell the truth and to say what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you agree with this proposition taken from the evidence of the FARK senior commander - transcript 7642, line 23, in the previous trial - would you agree with this proposition: that after the 12th July Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Zemaj became closer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment they were close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now on the 20th of July, was there a swearing-in ceremony for the troops that had recently arrived, from under the FARK banner, held in Vranoc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please ask the question again? I'm not sure I understood it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm suggesting to you that the newly arrived FARK soldiers, together with other volunteers, were all called to a large swearing-in ceremony in Vranoc on the 20th of July, which is recorded, as it happens, on video-tape and available to the Tribunal. Presumably you yourself were at that swearing-in ceremony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And presiding over that swearing-in ceremony were Tahir Zemaj and Mr. Haradinaj jointly, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, they both addressed the troops, didn't they? That was -- it was a very public moment when it became clear that both forces had integrated. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you I don't remember. I do know that I was present, but I don't remember what you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you saying that even then you didn't realize that the two forces had integrated into joint brigades? Even at the swearing-in ceremony you didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that that was a continuation of Brigade 134 and that these two other brigades were formed in the wake of that. This is all I know. You are asking me about what I know, not about what others have said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you because you've told us were at the joint swearing-in ceremony, and we have a video of that ceremony available to the Tribunal. So I'm asking you to be very careful in your evidence, Witness 77. Are you saying that even by the time of that swearing-in ceremony you didn't realize that the two forces had integrated into one?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The witness has answered that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He absolutely hasn't answered it. The last answer is non-responsive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or did you not know on the 20th when you attended a joint swearing-in ceremony at which both forces jointly took the oath of allegiance to Mr. Zemaj and Mr. Haradinaj jointly -- are you telling us you still didn't know then that the two forces had already integrated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you I don't remember that Haradinaj and Zemaj were present. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before you asked my this last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I know that was not your question. But your question has something new in it which I just want to verify with you. You say this was a joint swearing-in ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So both forces came -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... forces, yes. Into a single unified force, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- I even notice in the same regard that you said to the witness, you asked -- you said to the witness, line 5, page 75 [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You've told us you were at a joint swearing-in ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That is not -- that is definitely what the witness told. The went didn't say joint.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That may be a slip of the tongue. It is a joint swearing-in ceremony. There is no conceivable dispute on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me put it to you this way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry. The question is whether the witness knew or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, he's told us he didn't know Mr. Haradinaj was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that by the time of that swearing-in ceremony you still did not know that these two forces had integrated into one, under the command of Mr. Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did or you did not, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Didn't. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- did you ever become aware much later in August that there came a time when Mr. Zemaj took over from Mr. Haradinaj as commander of the Dukagjini zone following the Serbian offensive in Gllogjan at the end of August? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you knew that Mr. Zemaj took over as commander from Mr. Haradinaj at the end of July, is it the position that until then you didn't know that Mr. Haradinaj was the commander of Tahir Zemaj? Sorry, I think that there is a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never knew that Haradinaj was the commander of Zemaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the time when you were at that swearing-in ceremony, you knew, did you not, that Mr. Haradinaj was the commander of the KLA forces in the Dukagjini region, into which your force had entered? You knew that at least.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I knew. But I also knew that never did Brigade 134, to my recollection, enter under Haradinaj's command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I said. You knew that he was the commander of the KLA. At the swearing-in ceremony, were you all being sworn in to one force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you earlier, that brigade was formed as a continuation of Brigade 134 with that senior commander, whose name I don't want to mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the swearing-in ceremony, were you all being sworn in to one force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had already taken my oath much earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put the question another way. Those who were sworn in at the swearing-in ceremony, were they all being sworn in to one force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you think -- what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all being sworn in as soldiers of the UCK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, to your knowledge, who was the commander of the UCK in the Dukagjini plain on the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you still say you didn't realize they were a combined force, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you that, to my recollection, that brigade was the continuation of Brigade 134. If you want to put something else to me and if you want me to say things to please you, that's something else. I'm telling you what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mm-hm?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I just want to clarify something with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The question and answer that appears at page 58, lines 23 and following, the question, Mr. Witness, that Mr. Emmerson asked was: "At the swearing-in ceremony, were you all being sworn in to one force?" And your answer was that: "I had already taken my oath much earlier." Do I understand that to mean that you personally didn't take part in this ceremony, that you were just an observer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: What was the -- what, then, was the -- how was the distinction made about -- between those who, like you, may have taken their oaths earlier and were just observing, and those who were sworn in on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see any difference between that swearing in and the one I experienced earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is right, isn't it, Witness 77, that those present at that swearing-in ceremony who did take the oath included the soldiers who had come with you into Kosovo under the FARK banner, or under the FARK command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, so that we're clear, then, before we go into private session to deal with the particular incident that arose, I just want to look, then, briefly with you at dates again. We know that you, the FARK forces, entered to Isniq on the 30th of June, and I'm going to suggest to you, and I think you agree with that, that following the meeting on the 10th of July agreement was reached between the commanders, Mr. Zemaj and Mr. Haradinaj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was a period between the 30th of June and the 10th of July, a period of just under two weeks, when you, your forces, were inside Kosovo without an agreement having been reached; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But after the 10th of July agreement was reached. And whether they were integrated or not, the two forces were fighting side by side; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never saw them side by side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... a literal translation. The two forces were fighting in agreement with one another against a common enemy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe there was agreement, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... you did know. I don't understand, Witness, why you are fencing over these issues, why you are being so defensive about --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: He said, "There was an agreement, but I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. In which case I apologise for the comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, but what doesn't he know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... can I say I know if I don't know something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I get clarification here. Sir, you say you do know that there was agreement on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know whether, from the 10th of July onwards, FARK and KLA were fighting as allies against a common enemy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To my recollection, the territory was divided into two parts, from Bistrica and Lluke, and further on it was under Haradinaj's command. From Bistrica, on this part, it was under FARK's command. This is how I know it. I can't say something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... that may be so, sir. But do you know whether even this division of the territory was by agreement so that the two forces fight together, one covering the other area -- the one area and the other covering another area, but they were allies, facing a common enemy? Do you know that as a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. There was an agreement about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I ought to make it clear: I'm not going to press this with the witness because of the answers that he's given. But the Defence case and the Prosecution case, based on the exhibits that have been adduced and called at the previous trial, is that thereafter there was an amalgamation. But leaving that aside, on this witness's own understanding, as a very minimum, the two forces were allies fighting a common enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so what I want to do, then, is to focus with you on the fact that there was a period of approximately two weeks, just under two weeks, during which the FARK forces were inside western Kosovo but where the agreement about their deployment had not been made and there was a disagreement between the commanders. That's an accurate reflection, isn't it, that during that two-week period between 30th June and the 10th of July there was conflict between the commanders of deployment, and you knew that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was in that context and against that background that the incident took place about which we've heard evidence in private session. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we now go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We will take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson -- I beg your pardon. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Mr. Emmerson. Yeah, closed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. I presume, Mr. Emmerson, you'd like to revert to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: After one or two questions in open session, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 77, you remained in Kosovo until September 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were one of the soldiers who remained under the direct command of Tahir Zemaj's brigade, you've told us, is that correct, during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Tahir Zemaj's brigade engaged in a number of battles with Serb forces between the 10th of July and early September. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including, notably, a distinguished victory in Lloxha?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you fight in Lloxha?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you fight in any of the battles that took place under Tahir Zemaj's command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we turn to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember me asking you some questions earlier on today about the swearing-in ceremony at Vranoc which you attended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember you telling the Tribunal that you didn't recognise Ramush Haradinaj there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I don't remember that he was there present. This is what I said. Not that I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can I just play you, please, two passages of video-tape from that swearing-in ceremony. And just for your assistance and for the Bench's assistance, I'm going to suggest to you afterwards that the first commander we see speaking and inspecting the troops is Tahir Zemaj, and I'm going to ask you to confirm whether I'm correct about that or not. And then I'm going to ask you some questions about the other people who appear on the platform alongside him. Two short excerpts from this piece of video-tape. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We don't have the script for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause for a moment. Just pause the footage for a minute. We don't -- the words don't matter. We can play it without sound, if need be. It's the people who are attending that matter. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's the first extract. Now, pause for a moment before you play the second. Can we go into private session for a moment please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we play the second extract, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first officer we see there speaking, that is the senior FARK commander, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we talking about this one, this person here?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause it, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it is who's speaking there to the -- to the recruits, as the other commander in charge addressing the troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's Mr. Haradinaj, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who's the man standing at the end of the line of three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tahir Zemaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we've got the senior FARK commander introducing Mr. Haradinaj, who is standing on the platform, together with Tahir Zemaj, jointly addressing the troops. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. But I didn't remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll just see how long it went on for so that you can explain to us how you might have forgotten what, I suggest, would have been a very significant moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now, just so that we're clear, I suggested to you earlier on that this was a joint swearing-in ceremony in which the commanders of the two forces welcomed an integrated force, and you told us that you had no idea, even then, that the two forces had combined; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yet you tell us that you recognised and knew that the man on the platform was the leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army in the Dukagjin plain, who had, you tell us, you thought, opposed the entry of the FARK forces into Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this must have been a very significant moment, wouldn't you agree, to see the two commanders standing side by side, jointly welcoming recruits into the same integrated force? It must have been a very significant moment for you, because it changed your perception of what was going on, surely, if you recognised it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how long it took, because in a video you can't reflect all the events that took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. If you recognised this man as Ramush Haradinaj, a man who you say at that time you thought had opposed the entry of the FARK officers and soldiers into Kosovo, standing side by side with your revered commander, Tahir Zemaj, and jointly addressing the troops together with the senior FARK commander, you must have appreciated that something significant was taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, is this a correct summary of what the witness is supposed to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Didn't he know about the agreement that was reached on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He also told us unequivocally that at the time of this joint swearing-in ceremony he had no idea - and he's just confirmed it - that this was an integrated force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But that's -- that's totally different.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let me put the question totally differently then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 77, you must have realized that it was a significant moment to see Ramush Haradinaj standing on a podium with Tahir Zemaj jointly addressing the troops, mustn't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has said he doesn't recall Ramush Haradinaj was at this swearing-in ceremony, so I don't believe this question is correctly stating the testimony of the witness so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. Let me put a different question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen the two together before, jointly addressing troops as commanders in alliance with one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On reflection, do you accept that this was a significant moment to have the two of them on the same platform, jointly welcoming recruits into the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I said even earlier, but I don't know how long it lasted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... you accept that it was a significant moment, to see the two of them together?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Emmerson, I think the witness's testimony, even before this was played, was that he doesn't remember Ramush Haradinaj being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So -- so when you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's exactly the point I'm seeking to probe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: One -- one -- if an event of monumental significance of this kind takes place, one would expect him to remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If his recognition is reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me tell you what I'm trying to say to you. And I notice you, Madam Kravetz. You're saying to the witness that -- "Had you ever seen the two together before, jointly addressing troops as commanders in alliance with one another," and he said "no." On reflection, do you accept that this was a significant moment to have the two of them on the same platform jointly welcoming recruits into the KLA. And he says, yes, I said even earlier. But I don't know how long it lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, he means: I don't know how long the video lasted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- in relation to the entirety of the swearing-in ceremony. He's jumping to my next question, which is: How could you conceivably have forgotten?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just be clear: You've accepted, I think, Witness 77, that it was a very significant moment to have the two commanders addressing the troops jointly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And however long it was that Mr. Haradinaj spoke for, are you suggesting to me that the officers on the ground didn't realize that this was a joint command?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I don't believe that's what the witness has said. Maybe Mr. Emmerson -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's a question. He's not being asked whether he said so. He's just being asked the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put the question again. Are you suggesting that the officers on the ground did not realize that the commander of the Dukagjini KLA and the commander of the FARK forces were operating as a joint command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before the witness answers - and I'm sorry to interfere - I don't think he can speak on behalf the other -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did he -- let me put this question a different way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'd seen this, Witness 77, would you have realized that the two commanders were now operating jointly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what would you have made of it then? Swearing soldiers into the same force, under the same emblem of the KLA, with them being welcomed and addressed by Tahir Zemaj, the senior FARK commander, and Ramush Haradinaj, on the same platform. How would you have interpreted those events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you listen to their statements, they are contrary to one another. Then you can understand that there is nothing in common between them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I will look at some other documents, then, if that's your answer. Because we can deal with the transcript of the video in due course. But if your suggestion is that they were continuing to operate as separate forces, let's look at some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 65 ter 192, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you can see, can you not, that that is a request addressed to the Dukagjini plain operational staff and signed by Tahir Zemaj. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so he's requesting something of somebody, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any more senior FARK officer inside Kosovo at that time than Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know, don't you, that the Dukagjini plain operative staff was the staff of which Ramush Haradinaj was then titular head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this Mr. Zemaj requesting Mr. Haradinaj to authorise certain action. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It seems like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's look at what he's requesting: "Pursuant to the 10th July 1998 agreement," that's the day of the incident you've told us about in the barracks at Prapaqan, "we," that is, your commander, "hereby request the appointment and job specifications of military officers in the operative brigades." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we can see various people listed there, including Mr. Zemaj himself, asking to be appointed as the officer in charge of infantry. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... down a little. He's also asking, at 8, that Shemsedin Ceku be appointed as an officer in charge of infantry; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know who Shemsedin Ceku is, don't you? He was a leader of a subzone, a subzone commander of the KLA before you entered Kosovo, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you're asking the question and answering the question yourself. But, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you to agree with the proposition. Number 18: Mr. Zemaj is asking for the appointment of Rrustem Tetaj. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Skender Rexhahmetaj, who's given evidence in this trial; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Gani Gjukaj, you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were all KLA commanders operating within the Dukagjin zone before FARK entered, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The names that I've just read out to you. Shemsedin Cekaj, Driton Zeneli, Rrustem Tetaj, Skender Rexhahmetaj, and Gani Gjukaj. Those men. They were all KLA commanders before you came in, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those three or four, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereas the others, of course, were FARK officers, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document in which Mr. Zemaj's asking Mr. Haradinaj to agree the appointment of officers in a combined forces, some from FARK and some from KLA, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It is not within the scope of knowledge of this witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He can tell us -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what this document is, isn't it? Do you want me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, please, if you can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: This is a request from Tahir Zemaj to Ramush Haradinaj to agree the appointment of officers, some from FARK and some from the KLA, into a joint force, as a result of the 10th of July agreement. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you earlier that I don't agree. Not that I don't agree per se, but I don't know about these facts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's ask about your own brigade, which you presumably do know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look at P245, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's dated the 12th of July. And we've got only one page on the English translation. But can you see, can't you, that in the Albanian it is signed by Mr. Haradinaj. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's an authorisation signed by Mr. Haradinaj which reads as follows. First of all, I should say this: It is addressed to Mr. Zemaj. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says: "Due to the restructuring of combat formations and operative means to establish the desired leadership, command ... control, subordination, and the completion of war tasks, I," that is, Mr. Haradinaj, "... authorise officer Tahir Zemaj to form the first brigade ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's your brigade, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The formation of which was authorised by Mr. Haradinaj following the request we've just seen from Mr. Zemaj. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you earlier I'm not aware of these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... about whether you were aware of them. I'm asking about whether you agree that that's what they say, that the brigade that were yourself a part of and which you've given evidence about, and you've been called by the Prosecution to tell the Trial Chamber about FARK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Interpretation, please. I'm not receiving any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me now in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You understand that you've been called by the Prosecution to give evidence about relationship, in part, between FARK and the KLA. You've been asked lots of questions about that by Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, only a few questions were asked of me about this. We mostly spoke about the incidents that happened than about the relationships between the FARK and the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You repeatedly volunteered the opinion that Mr. Haradinaj was obstructive and seeking to prevent the FARK from entering. And you expressed the opinion that so far as you were aware these forces remained separate. That's your testimony. And so I'm inviting you to comment on your own brigade that you've told us all about, headed by Mr. Zemaj. What I'm suggesting to you is that Zemaj was appointed as commander of that brigade by Mr. Haradinaj. Do you agree or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that. I already told you so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the light of what you've seen, do you agree that you must have been under a misapprehension then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the light of what these documents prove, do you accept that you were under a misapprehension about the relationship between the two forces of which you were a part? Or one of which you were a part of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were orders from both sides, I think. However, as I told you, I can't remember. I don't remember whether there was agreement for the formation of these brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look at P242, please. P242. Another of the brigades. This one dated the 11th of July, signed by Mr. Haradinaj, and authorising Shemsedin Cekaj to form the 2nd Brigade. So we're now dealing with the 2nd Brigade. And the 2nd Brigade contained FARK soldiers and officers, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about documents now, Witness 77. You know that the 2nd Brigade, which included soldiers and officers who'd come into Kosovo with you under the FARK authority, you knew that the 2nd Brigade that was formed, the time that you were part of the 1st Brigade, was a brigade that included FARK officers and soldiers, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The witness has answered the question. He said that he was not aware of that. That's at line 22 of page 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He said: I don't know these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you: Did you know that the 2nd Brigade contained FARK soldiers an officers?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt again, but the first part of that answer says "I'm not aware" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's clarify what the witness meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say -- did you know that the 2nd Brigade contained FARK soldiers and officers or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This the first time I hear this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we then, please, look at P248, because this is the formation of the 2nd Brigade's personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you've told us a little bit about some of these people already.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: P248, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, dated the 12th of July and following on from the 10th of July meeting. And you can see at paragraph 2 that Mr. Haradinaj has appointed Shemsedin Cekaj as commander. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who are the first two names on the list as Chief of Staff and commander of the 1st Battalion? Shaban Dragaj and Musa Gjakova; do you see those names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... about those two men, and you told us you knew that they were part of the FARK officer corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So does it follow that you knew that two of the FARK officer corps were from the 12th of July under the command of Shemsedin Cekaj, a KLA commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. I know that Musa Gjakova was commander of 133rd Brigade in Palabardhe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Driton Zeneli is, the third name on the list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I've heard this name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you'd accept from me, would you, that what this document shows is that the two senior FARK officers who you were fully aware of, because you told us this morning you knew that they were FARK officers, were, according to this document, under the command of Shemsedin Cekaj, from the 12th of July? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was their commander then, please, these two senior officers that you say you know, Shaban Dragaj and Musa Gjakova? Who did you understand to be their commander; and which brigade did you understand them to be a part of, yours or another one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see Shaban Dragaj and Musa Gjakova. Musa Gjakova was an appointed -- a commander appointed by Tahir Zemaj in the Palabardhe area, while Ramabaja was commander of the 131st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the position is that these documents -- and you've seen one -- a request signed by your own commander, Tahir Zemaj, requesting this allocation or this series of allocations. If these documents properly reflect what they say, then you would agree, wouldn't you, that the two forces were amalgamated from the 12th of July onwards under a joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. I don't know. I can't say I agree with something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And right -- that remained the position right up to the moment when, on the 20th of July, you yourself saw them jointly on a platform receiving recruits into a joint force, did it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't recall the witness saying that he saw them jointly on a platform receiving recruits.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We've just looked at a video-tape of an incident, an event, at which this witness was present, in which both Mr. Zemaj and Mr. Haradinaj took an oath of allegiance from the troops on the 20th of July at Vranoc, in which the witness says he was present.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The witness has said -- the question is framed with the date of "... 20th of July, you yourself saw some them jointly," and the witness has indicated that he does not recall Mr. Haradinaj being at that -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think you're -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... that you were present, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Emmerson. You're going to make a distinction between what the witness saw now on the -- on the video and what he told us he saw on the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Essentially, Witness 77, you would have the Tribunal believe that all of this amalgamation simply passed you by and you knew nothing about it, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think these things you're showing to me here are illogical. I was not aware of them. With regard to the swearing-in ceremony, it is possible that another officer and myself arrived there later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say, that it was not possible for me to see those commanders, the senior commanders, there earlier. That's why I repeated over and over again that I can't remember them -- him being there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in order to reconcile your testimony, we have to understand it this way: That on the 9th of July you arrived at Prapaqan late, just after the forces had arrived, because that's the only way to reconcile your testimony, and on the 20th of July you arrived at the swearing-in ceremony, you managed to catch enough of it to see the swearing-in but didn't see the speeches that we've just seen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That is not a correct statement of the witness evidence. What he just said was that it was -- that it is possible that he arrived -- I'm looking for the exact passage -- he arrived late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testimony, as I understand it, is that you didn't see the speeches - is that right or not? - at the Vranoc swearing in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Had I seen them, I would have said so. But I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you must have missed the speeches at Vranoc and arrived at Prapaqan on the 9th of July, just in time to miss the arrival of the forces. That's the effect of your testimony, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the moment, we're speaking about Baran. I did not watch the speeches. I did not see Haradinaj or Zemaj holding any speeches there. This is what I know and what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing there then? I thought you'd come to watch the swearing-in ceremony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was just escorting an officer to Baran. Because he was not from that area and he did not know the way to Baran, so he asked me to escort him up to Baran, and I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question from Judge Hall, you said that you were -- having been sworn in yourself on an earlier occasion, you were there to watch. Did you have to take that officer there in time for him to be sworn in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He said he had been invited but he didn't know where the place was, so I helped him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you arrive late, then, you and this officer who you were taking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see the speeches.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you want me to say that I saw them when I didn't, that's a different matter. I'm saying I did not see the speeches. Whether I was late or not, I can't precisely tell you. What I can tell you is that I was not there for the speeches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It would, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Court adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, 28th day of September, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
